rv.q: What's inevitably lost is the excitement of watching a single performer act the chameleon, flipping between characters as if changing psychic TV channels. But what's gained in the new staging, directed by Whitney White, is the warm camaraderie of an ensemble work.
This sterling revival demonstrates that, with the right actors and creative talent, The Whoopi Monologues is strong enough to make an impact without its namesake star.
Young (Purlie Victorious, Purpose) is flawless, whether discussing the Anne Frank house in Amsterdam, eyes full of wonder, or describing the airplane meal.
It's quite a show, but not quite as impressive as watching one talented actor perform all five roles.
The evening ultimately feels like less than the sum of its parts.

cn.t: This revival showcases Goldberg's sharp writing and social commentary through five talented performers, proving her original material remains potent even when divided among multiple actors rather than delivered as a solo showcase.
